0.0.n: A playful, rustic way to say I, characteristic of this speaker.

0.1.n: Links オラ to 映画 to show whose movies they are.

0.2.n: Japanese nouns do not distinguish singular from plural; here it refers to multiple movies.

0.3.n: Marks the movies as what is reaching its thirtieth anniversary.

0.4.n: 周年 counts years since something began, rather than someone's age.

0.5.n: Combines with 30周年 to describe celebrating the anniversary.

0.6.n: Marks the anniversary commemoration as the occasion for the release.

0.7.n: This is the first part of ブルーレイ, split across two subtitle tokens.

0.8.n: Completes ブルーレイ, the name of the disc format; it is not a separate word here.

0.9.n: Marks ブルーレイ as what is being released.

0.10.n: A noun announcing that the Blu-rays are going on sale.

0.11.n: The casual form of です, used after the noun 発売.

0.12.n: An emphatic sentence ending, written in katakana here for the speaker's playful style.

1.0.n: 懐かしい describes fond feelings about the past; です adds politeness.

1.1.n: The stretched ね invites agreement and makes the comment sound warmly reflective.

2.0.n: Points to the period being shown or discussed and must come before a noun.

2.1.n: Refers to an approximate period rather than an exact moment.

2.2.n: Links この頃 to オラ, describing the speaker as he was at that time.

2.3.n: The speaker's playful, rustic self-reference; here he is talking about his earlier self.

2.5.n: Softens the description of being heavy.

2.6.n: 重たい becomes 重たくない in the negative; rising intonation asks for agreement rather than denying heaviness.

3.0.n: Gives the duration over which the releases will happen.

3.1.n: The て-form of かける connects the time spent to the release process.

3.2.n: 発売する becomes 発売して, then adds いく to show the releases continuing forward over time.

3.3.n: Adds confident emphasis to this casual announcement, with playful katakana spelling.

0.lit: My movies, for their thirtieth-anniversary commemoration, Blu-rays are going on sale, I tell you!
0.tip: 記念で presents the anniversary celebration as the occasion for the Blu-ray release.

1.tip: ねぇ invites the listener to share the speaker's nostalgic feeling.

2.lit: The me of this time, wasn't I a little heavy?
2.tip: この頃のオラ means the speaker as he was in the period being shown.

3.lit: Taking one year, we'll go on releasing them, I tell you!
3.tip: ていく shows the releases unfolding over time, rather than happening all at once.
